Usage

Exact signed distance field of a half-space (the side cut off by a plane) (negative inside, positive outside).

sdf(p) = (p - point) · n̂. The side the normal n̂ points to is outside (positive), the opposite side inside. Used for operations that keep only one side, such as chamfering, cutting, or "only above the substrate". Stacking sdf_intersect builds any convex polyhedron. However, intersection by max is not exact outside the corners: building a cuboid from 6 planes, the occupancy (<= 0) and the inside values match box_sdf exactly, but outside it underestimates near the corners by up to 2.1 (measured on a box of half side 2, grid 0.25) —— a standard property of CSG; if the distance itself is needed, use box_sdf.

Exactness: a plane has gradient norm 1 in all of space, so this value is the true signed distance everywhere (no case split that switches at corners as in box_sdf is needed).

Arguments and validation (ValueError):

• grid: float array (..., 3) whose last axis is 3 (output of grid_coords or a point list).

• point: 1 point on the plane (3 elements).

• normal: normal of the plane (3 elements; zero vector and NaN are rejected). Its length is normalised to 1 automatically, so the magnitude does not affect the result (only the direction matters).

Return value: float64 of grid.shape[:-1]. Positive on the normal side, negative on the opposite side, 0 on the plane.

Usage: sdf_subtract(part, plane_sdf(g, p, n)) "cuts away the normal side of that plane". To reverse the direction, flip the sign of normal (-sdf gives the same).

The 3d op plane_sdf bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). This op has no tunable parameters; neither a nor b is used.
